gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Bloody swings in with big round lowercase bowls and a commanding, slightly menacing look, while Noto Sans Khojki keeps its exits wide enough to let light through. Over a long page, that sans stays modern and easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Noto Sans Khudawadi sits low and friendly, its capitals barely above the lowercase and its rounds left open like an unlatched hook. Bloody earns its keep big and short, where those round bowls can look commanding.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-kr: Huge round bowls in the lowercase give Bloody a commanding, slightly menacing face. And Noto Sans KR, a plain sans with stubby ascenders and generous gaps in its curves, gives the page somewhere to rest.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-lao: Bloody's big round lowercase bowls make a commanding, bloody statement up top. Then Noto Sans Lao follows with a tall x-height and open mouths, so a long passage reads smoothly and modern.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-lao-loope: Heavy, bowl-shaped menace up top, then a quiet turn. Bloody brings the commanding drama, but Noto Sans Lao Looped turns words into solid blocks, which makes the sans-serif body feel modern and sure.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Commanding is how Bloody looks, all big round bowls, and Noto Sans Lepcha stands beside it with a lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals. Giving the heading plenty of size lets that contrast with the sans show.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Approachable is the word for the body here, though Bloody up top is commanding, with big round bowls that look almost bloody. Noto Sans Limbu, a plain sans with tall-bodied small letters, reads easily.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu has tiny gaps between its ascender tops and the x-height line, plus wide-open s curves that feel professional. Shrink Bloody and its commanding bowls lose their menace, whereas Noto Sans Lisu holds up fine as plain sans text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian keeps its capitals barely above the lowercase, with openings wide as a sprung paper clip. Bloody is the one to make a loud, commanding entrance, while the sans quietly handles the steady reading.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Bloody is all big round bowls and swagger. Noto Sans Mahajani stands tall against its capitals and flares a funnel-wide throat in the e, which makes the sans-serif body the pair's most welcoming quality.
